patch.value:
## What happens

When a tracker item exists under the ID the importer reserves for an issue (`<prefix>-github-<hash>-<N>`) but was not created by the importer, the gated import refuses to run for the whole repository:

> GitHub import target pm-vcs-github-c1741e698b48-228 is reserved for unbraind/pm-vcs#228, but its current owner is curated/unowned for content mirroring; importer creation provenance missing. Restore the intended GitHub provenance only if this item belongs to that issue; otherwise use a different configured ID prefix or tracker. …

This happened in three repositories on 2026-11-26 (pm-vcs issue 228, pm-rl issue 202, pm-ado issue 137): while the sync was down, agents that fixed those issues created the tracker item by hand under the reserved ID and tagged it `gh:owner/repo#N`.

## What works (verified)

Setting the declared field on the item links it explicitly, and the import then matches it by provenance:

```
pm update <item> --field github_url=https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<N>
pm github import <owner>/<repo> --state all --atomic --gate --dry-run   # plan verified, 1 matched by provenance
```

`--adopt-cited` alone does not help, and `pm github identity --identity … --owner …` needs a `--detach`, which does not fit a single item.

## Expected

1. The refusal names the repair: "set `github_url` on this item to link it, or …".
2. The documentation for people and agents who start work on an issue says how to get its item: `pm github import <owner>/<repo> --issue <N>` (creates it with provenance), never a hand-created item under the reserved ID form.
3. Optional: `pm create` refuses or warns when the requested ID matches the importer's reserved form and no `github_url` is set.

## Acceptance

- The refusal text contains the repair command for the named item.
- Tests: a hand-created item under the reserved ID with `github_url` set is matched; without it the refusal names the repair.
A hand-created item under the importer's reserved ID stops the whole sync, and the refusal does not name the repair

value.author: pi-glm
value.text:
Re-review round 1 blocked the PR with three findings; continuing on the same branch, PR and item. Plan per finding, closing the class not the line:

1. Repair command without the failing invocation's tracker selector (import-repair): general rule - a rendered repair command must replay the caller's tracker scope, like the host's revision-recovery scopeArgs. Fix: the reserved-ID repair command includes the tracker selector the failed import used, so copying it from any directory updates only that tracker. Search: every rendered repair/example command in the package that writes to a tracker item gets the same scope treatment.

2. Repair offered on incomplete provenance (import-repair): general rule - a repair is offered only when applying it leaves exactly one consistent GitHub owner, evaluated with the same ownership-claims machinery the next import uses. Fix: the refusal carries the refused item snapshot and the offer is withheld unless the post-link claims are exactly the target issue. Search: every other adoption/link suggestion for the same precondition.

3. Comment mirror stores source timestamps unvalidated (comment-mirror): general rule - external source timestamps are validated before persistence, like the importer's source-lifetime gate; a malformed value must count as a failed write and stay retryable, never be stored and skipped by marker. Search: every other path that persists source-provided timestamps.

Non-blocking CodeRabbit out-of-scope check: factually wrong - the comment-mirror requirements are stated in issue #286's first comment (the non-convergent linked-item mirror), which this PR fixes alongside the reserved-ID refusal by design; the suggested alternative (link an issue that states the comment requirements) is already satisfied by that comment. Will strengthen the PR body's explicit link to it.

value.author: pi-glm
value.text:
Round-1 blocking findings implemented on the same branch; no second PR, no new item.

1. Scope replay: a new invocation scope (AsyncLocalStorage, same pattern the host uses for its own recovery scope) captures the typed tracker selector at the four command registrations that can render invocation-bound commands (github/gh-issues import, refresh, webhooks reconcile). The reserved-ID repair now renders pm --pm-path <the failing invocation's own spelling> update <id> --field github_url=<url>, matching the host's revision-recovery convention: replay the typed selector verbatim, keep an implicit (cwd/PM_PATH) selection implicit so a same-shell copy resolves the same tracker. Class search found two more invocation-bound rendered commands and fixed both the same way: the comment-mirror ownership-conflict release example (comment-mirror.ts) and the webhook reconcile recovery hint (webhooks.ts).

2. Safe-link predicate: the curated/unowned refusal now carries the refused item snapshot non-enumerably (never serialized into diagnostics), and the link offer is kept only when the item's post-link ownership claims are exactly the target issue, evaluated with the same githubOwnershipClaims the next import uses. A reserved item with a contradicting github_number or github_repo keeps the plain refusal, so the offered repair can never create contradictory ownership that blocks the next import.

3. Timestamp validation: the mirror validates each source comment timestamp before any write; a missing or unparseable one is counted failed and retried on the next sync, never stored and never skipped by its marker id. Item-level source lifetimes already had this rule (validateImportLifetime); the comment mirror was the one unvalidated persistence path in the package.

Revert proofs (behavioral reverts in a disposable copy, restored and re-verified green after each):

- Scope revert: rendering the repair without the invocation's selector failed the tracker-scoped regression at the first assertion, with the refusal showing the bare pm update command. Restored: pass.
- Provenance revert: dropping the post-link claims predicate made the refusal offer the link to the item carrying github_number=8, failing 'a link that would create contradictory ownership must not be offered'. Restored: pass.
- Timestamp revert: storing comment.created_at unvalidated counted the three malformed comments as added=4/failed=0 and wrote malformed rows, failing the deep-equal. Restored: pass.
- With all fixes restored the full linked-import regression file passes 8/8 in the disposable copy.

One existing fixture needed its comment timestamp made valid, not a weakened assertion: coverage-remainder's metadata-preservation and read-only-directory tests used created_at empty strings as don't-care values; each now carries a valid source timestamp so the same write paths are still exercised (the read-only failure still fails at the write; the metadata row still lands). The body-mode builder tests keep their empty timestamps because body text is mirrored content, not persisted metadata.

Gates so far: typecheck, build, test build, lint, docstring (328 declarations), duplication (34 modules, zero clones), privacy (10654 objects audited), the ownership inventory regenerated and verified (one new classified group for the repair renderer), and the packed minimum-SDK consumer (2026.10.23) passed. Focused regressions: linked-import 8/8; comments-sync/import-ownership/ownership-consistency/import-errors/scoped-ownership 208; webhooks/workflow-diagnostic/cited-adoption/import-lock/legacy-description/owner-field-values 121; round-seventeen/eighteen/twelve/sdk-adoption 41; coverage-remainder 25; identity-inventory 9; coverage-edges 9; minimum-sdk 1. A full 100-file local run was stopped at the 90-minute mark after an npm EALLOWSCRIPTS flake in strict-import-admission under two-worker concurrency; that file passes 2/2 standalone and unchanged thresholds remain for CI.

value.author: pi-glm
value.text:
Round-2 non-blocking findings, closed as a class on the same branch (merged the v2026.11.26 release first; the release touched only version files and CHANGELOG, no tracker overlap):

1+4. Calendar-invalid timestamps (comment-mirror guard and its test corpus). General rule: a persisted source timestamp must name a real calendar moment, never a normalized rollover - JavaScript date parsing accepts impossible dates (2026-02-30 rolls to March 2) and free-form strings (February 31, 2026). Fix: a new pure module (source-time.ts) admits only RFC 3339 timestamps whose declared fields read back exactly; both persistence paths that store provider times now use it - the comment mirror (annotation writes) and the importer's source-lifetime gate (validateImportLifetime, item lifetimes), the one other instance of the same rule found by the search. Checked and exempt: blocker markers render dates as text, body-mode comment text is mirrored content, closeout reads SDK-written local timestamps, durable state writes generated times. Real leap days stay importable (2028-02-29 accepted); non-leap 2027-02-29, 2026-02-30, February 31 and 2/31/2026 are refused in both the mirror and the lifetime corpus.

2. Cross-directory claim in the repair doc. General rule: guidance states the limits of its own copy safety. The doc now distinguishes the three selector forms (typed selector repeats and is relative-safe only from its directory; implicit selection stays shell-bound; only an absolute selector is safe from any directory) and qualifies the unscoped example. The docs test pins the qualified sentences.

3. Atomic rethrow path (index.ts). Factually wrong, not fixed as code: createPmCliExpectedError DOES mirror context.code onto a top-level code property - verified empirically against the pinned SDK and by source against the declared 2026.10.23 floor (src/core/shared/errors.ts: this.code = context.code), so both atomic rethrow guards match the wrapped repair refusal and rethrow it unchanged. Proof: a new deterministic regression injects the commitAtomic dependency so the reserved item appears between the import's planning and its transaction, and the surfaced refusal keeps code github_import_owner_conflict, exit code 2 and the leading repair guidance. Reverting to the finding's failure mode (stripping the code from the wrapped error) makes that test fail with the generic transaction wrap burying the repair - so any real instance of the claimed defect is now caught.

value.text: CI on the round-2 head failed the quick npm release gate's coverage threshold: the new source-time module had uncovered rejection branches (non-string input, negative offsets, out-of-range zone offsets) and the fraction-less epoch disagreed with the engine on fractional seconds. Fixed both: the parser now carries sub-second precision truncated to milliseconds exactly as the engine reads it, and a new property corpus test covers every branch - real RFC 3339 moments (Z, lowercase, fraction, both offset signs, leap days) agree with Date.parse, while non-strings, free forms, date-only, impossible calendar moments and out-of-range offsets are refused. The module now reports 100 percent statement, branch, function and line coverage locally; the linked-import, fidelity, comments-sync and coverage-remainder suites re-passed (103 tests). Pushing the fix.
